name: MCP3008
full_name: Microchip MCP3008 2.7V 8-Channel 10-Bit A/D Converter with SPI Serial Interface
description: The MCP3008 is a 10-bit successive-approximation ADC with eight multiplexed analog input channels and an SPI interface. Channels can be configured as eight single-ended inputs or four pseudo-differential pairs. It achieves up to 200 ksps at 5 V (75 ksps at 2.7 V) and uses an external reference voltage on VREF to set the full-scale range. Its simplicity, low cost, and clean SPI protocol made it the classic way to give a Raspberry Pi or other digital-only board analog inputs. The 16-pin part comes in PDIP, SOIC, and TSSOP.

pins.name: CS/SHDN
pins.description: Chip select / shutdown input; pull low to start communication, high between conversions

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: SPI serial data in; loads channel configuration

pins.name: DOUT
pins.description: SPI serial data out; conversion result, changes on falling SCLK edge

pins.name: SCLK
pins.description: SPI serial clock; initiates conversion and clocks out data

pins.name: VREF
pins.description: Reference voltage input; sets full-scale range

typical_application: Adding 8 channels of analog input to a digital-only host such as a Raspberry Pi via SPI.
gotchas: VREF is a separate external pin and sets full-scale; resolution per step is VREF/1024, so a noisy or low VREF directly degrades accuracy
VREF can be set independently of VDD but must not exceed VDD
CS/SHDN must be cycled high between conversions; leaving it low after a read can stall the next conversion
Has separate AGND (pin 14) and DGND (pin 9); tie them together at a single point near the device
The 14-pin MCP3004 is the 4-channel sibling with a different pinout (pins 5,6 are NC); do not interchange footprints
